newsitem.title: USA: ITT chief's 1996 compensation topped $5 mln.
newsitem.headline: ITT chief's 1996 compensation topped $5 mln.

text.p: ITT Corp's Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Rand Araskog earned just over $5 million last year, about half of what he earned the previous year when his compensation was bolstered by one-time payouts.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, ITT said Araskog's base salary remained unchanged at $2 million last year and his annual bonus slipped slightly to $2.26 million from $2.33 million in 1995.

In 1995, Araskog's compensation included $2.7 million in restricted stock awards and $2.63 million in long term incentive plan payouts. Those payments, coupled with his base salary and cash bonus, pushed his total 1995 compensation to $10.4 million.
In 1996, ITT said there were no awards of restricted stock or long term performance plan payments.

ITT said Araskog also received options on 150,000 shares of ITT stock in 1996, with an exercise price of $55.88 a share. If ITT's stock price rises five percent a year over the next 10 years, the options would be worth $5.3 million. If the stock rises 10 percent a year, the options would be worth $13.6 million.
ITT is currently the target of a hostile $6.5 billion bid by rival Hilton Hotels Corp.

ITT has rejected the offer and has embarked on a plan to sell non-core assets. Some analysts expect ITT to use the proceeds from the sale of the assets to pay for a special dividend or a share buyback.
